'''Valerie Saena Tuia''' is a plant scientist from Samoa.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://www.spc.int/70-inspiring-pacific-women/valerie-saena-tuia/|title=Valerie Saena Tuia|date=2017-09-20|work=Pacific Community|access-date=2018-07-11|language=en-US}}</ref> She served as Officer in Charge of the Genetic Resources at the [[Secretariat of the Pacific Community]] [[Centre for Pacific Crops and Trees]] for over 15 years, retiring in 2017.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://pacific.scoop.co.nz/2012/07/vulnerability-of-pacific-crops-addressed-by-cepact-2/|title=Vulnerability of Pacific crops addressed by CePaCT|website=pacific.scoop.co.nz|language=en|access-date=2018-07-11|date=July 31, 2012}}</ref>

== Life ==

Tuia holds a Bachelor of Agriculture, a postgraduate Diploma in Agriculture and a Masters in Agriculture.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Valerie_Tuia|title=Valerie TUIA Publications|website=ResearchGate|language=en|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-04-17}}</ref> In Samoa she held the positions of senior agricultural officer and principal research office in the Samoan civil service. In these roles she was responsible for working with farmers to assist them to diversify and improve their crops.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Community biodiversity management : promoting resilience and the conservation of plant genetic resources|date=2013|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-136-47487-3|editor-last=Boef, Walter de.|edition=1st|location=Abingdon}}</ref> She later moved to Fiji to work at the Secretariat of the Pacific Community Centre for Pacific Crops and Trees as officer in change of genetic resources.<ref name=":1" />

During her tenure, Tuia carried out scientific research into the root crop [[Colocasia esculenta|taro]], established the world's largest collection of taro and managed the region's plant genebank. The centre's collection of taro has been used to develop new varieties of taro tolerant to [[leaf blight]] disease.<ref name=":1" /> Tuia also worked on a system for propagating [[breadfruit]] which produced more vigorous and taller plants that those grown using conventional methods.<ref name=":0" />

Following her retirement, Tuia returned to Samoa to run a family business.<ref name=":0" />
